Registration name: MEIfaissel
rows.Origin:
Bred by Alain Meilland (1940-....) (France, before 2003).
Introduced in Japan by Keisei Rose Nurseries Inc. in 2004 as 'Oscar François'.
Introduced in United States by Star Roses & Plants (Pennsylvania) in 2005.
Introduced in Australia by Wagner's Rose Nursery in 2016 as 'Brilliance'.
rows.Bloom: Light yellow, orange-pink shading. Strong, apricot or peach, fruity, rose, sweet fragrance. up to 67 petals. Average diameter 5". Very large, very full (41+ petals), borne mostly solitary, in small clusters, cupped-to-flat bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season. Rounded buds.
rows.Habit:
Tall, upright. Semi-glossy, medium green, dense foliage. 3 to 7 leaflets.

Height: 39" to 5'11" (100 to 180cm). Width: 20" to 2' (50 to 60cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 7b and warmer. Can be used for beds and borders, container rose, cut flower, garden or landscape. Very hardy. very vigorous. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant. Remove spent blooms to encourage re-bloom. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that.

The female parent (i.e., the seed parent) was the `Meban` variety (non-patented in the United States). The `Meban` variety sometimes is known as the `White Knight` variety. The male parent (i.e., the pollen parent) was the product of the cross of the `Poulari` variety (U.S. Plant Pat. No. 9,274) and the `Lady Sylvia` variety (non-patented in the United States).
